extracted.intended_audience: typographers, typesetters, printers, book designers, and copy editors
extracted.subtask_description: A University of Chicago Press specimen book showing typefaces, sizes, ornaments, and associated style/index guidance for setting and editing text. The page combines type specimens (various faces, sizes, special characters, initials, ornaments, rules, borders) with index entries for editorial/typographic rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimens: show text in multiple point sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens display the same sample text set in a wide range of point sizes (examples on this page include 6, 8, 10, 11, 12, 14, 18, 20, 22, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 60, 72, 96, 120, 144, 180, 216).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each face/style, include the sample sentence at the common point sizes so readers can compare weight, proportion, and legibility across sizes; include both lowercase sentence and an uppercase line of the same sentence where shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show typefaces in multiple styles (roman, italic, bold, condensed, extended, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each face is shown in its available styles (e.g., Cheltenham, Cheltenham Italic, Cheltenham Bold Extra Condensed, Cheltenham Wide, Clarendon, Goudy Old Style, Goudy Bold, Gothic Condensed, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the same sample text across the different styles for direct visual comparison; include both regular and emphasized styles to illustrate differences in weight and width.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accented letters display
rubrics_metrics.description: Labelled 'ACCENTED LETTERS — SIX TO TWELVE POINT' (and similar), specimens include full sets of accented letters at specified sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include complete accented-letter samples at the small text sizes where accents are most challenging to render (commonly 6–12 point) so designers can evaluate clarity and diacritic placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special characters display
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries like 'SPECIAL CHARACTERS — ALL SIZES' and 'SPECIAL CHARACTERS — SIX TO TWELVE POINT' indicate inclusion of nonalphabetic glyphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide special characters and punctuation sets at relevant sizes (including small text sizes) so users can assess spacing, weight, and legibility of punctuation and symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures / numerals display (including advertising figures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens show numerals (e.g., '12345', '67890') and dedicated 'ADVERTISING FIGURES' sets at particular sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both text figures and advertising/lining figures at a variety of sizes to show numeral style, spacing, and suitability for display versus text use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initials (drop caps) specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections labelled 'INITIALS' show large-size initials (e.g., thirty-six, forty-eight, seventy-two point) and named initial designs (Burford, Della Robbia, Roycroft, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sample initial glyphs at large display sizes and show variants so book designers can choose complementary initial designs to pair with body type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ornaments and ornament numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: A long numbered sequence of 'ORNAMENTS' (with index numbers) provides decorative glyphs in multiple sets and sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a catalogued, numbered set of ornaments so users can reference and select ornament figures; display them at sizes appropriate for their intended use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Borders and border specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections labelled 'BORDERS' list numbered border designs with point-size indications (two-point, three-point, four-point, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show border variants and their recommended body/point sizes and give numbering so designers can reference particular border designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brass rule faces and rule styles
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 'BRASS RULE FACES' the specimen lists rule styles (hairline on one- and two-point body; dotted on one- or two-point body; hairline parallel on two-point body; half-point side face; one-point side face; two point, three point, four point).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document available rule widths and side-face treatments, and indicate which bodies they apply to; include examples so printers know how rules render at intended thicknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescription signs and specialized symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed as 'PRESCRIPTION SIGNS' among brass rule/ornament sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specialized symbol glyphs (e.g., prescription marks) in specimens so users can verify design and scale for specialized uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising / display figure variants (outline, shaded, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens include 'ADVERTISING FIGURES' and variants like 'THIRTY POINT OUTLINE' or 'TIFFANY SHADED'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show decorative figure styles (outline, shaded, shaded upright, etc.) at display sizes for advertising or decorative use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include combinations and small-combination faces
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries such as 'SIX POINT COMBINATION GOTHIC NO. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-THREE' indicate combination (composite) designs at small sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide combination faces intended for small-type settings and show how they reproduce at small sizes for legibility and aesthetic consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen layout: include both sentence and uppercase line
rubrics_metrics.description: For each specimen the same sentence appears twice—once in normal capitalization and once in all caps ('THE FIRST TIME THAT THE GRAND PROSPECT HAD BEEN HELD...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present both mixed-case and all-caps versions so readers can evaluate case-dependent metrics like line fit, letter-spacing, and optical weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include typeface family variations (wide, condensed, extra condensed, extended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many faces show family variations (e.g., Cheltenham Wide, Cheltenham Condensed, Cheltenham Bold Extra Condensed, Goudy Bold, Gothic Condensed, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display each family member with the same sample text and sizes to allow side-by-side comparison of width and weight within a family.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include special collections for typewriters and machine-set types
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections for 'REPRODUCING TYPEWRITER', 'NEW MODEL ELITE REMINGTON TYPEWRITER', 'REMINGTON TYPEWRITER' show how these mechanical types appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specimens of machine or typewriter faces, indicating how line breaks and spacing differ from hand-set types to inform layout decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index rule: provide cross-referenced editorial/typographic rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An index at the end lists editorial and typographic rules with section references (e.g., 'A and an: use of', 'Abbreviations', 'Accents', 'Academic degrees', etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a clear index mapping editorial/typographic topics to detailed sections so compositors and editors can find rules quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'A' and 'an' (article usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: '"A" and "an": use of, before h and ъ; spacing of, 268.' (index entry)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribe rules for when to use 'a' vs 'an' including special cases before 'h' and other phonetic considerations; include spacing guidance where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'a-' (negative particle) in compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: '"a-" (negative particle), compounds with;' (index entry pointing to guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rules for forming compounds with the negative particle 'a-' (hyphenation, spelling, and division rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations: spacing, division, punctuation and contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Index entry: 'Abbreviations: in literary references, no; of academic titles, 22; of biblical and apocryphal books, list of, 100; of directions, street names, locations of property, 1230; of names of states, 106; of technical terms, list of, in; of titles of publications, omission of period after initials used for, 1234,- rules for, 106-11; omission of period in, i23c; use of apostrophe in, 1236; when not to use, 105; of period after, 1230; no period after Mile, 123.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give comprehensive rules: when to use periods in abbreviations, spacing between abbreviation elements, whether abbreviations may be divided at line breaks, lists of standard abbreviations for specific contexts (biblical books, states, academic titles), and exceptions (e.g., no period after certain units).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation of '-able' and '-ible' in divisions
rubrics_metrics.description: '"-able" and "-ible," in divisions, 224.' (index entry)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify hyphenation and line-division rules for words ending in -able and -ible to guide correct breaking across lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic degrees: abbreviation and capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Academic degrees, abbreviation and capitalization of, 21-22.' (index entry)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rules for how to abbreviate and capitalize academic degrees (e.g., 'Ph.D.', 'M.A.'), including punctuation and spacing conventions in text and lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of accents in foreign words
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Accents, retention of, in foreign words incorporated into English, 59.' (index entry)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State when to retain original accents/diacritics in foreign borrowings versus anglicizing them, and note exceptions and typographic treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of words with acquired, limited, or special meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Acquired, limited, or special meaning, words having, capitalization of, 25.' (index entry)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define which specialized terms or words with technical/limited meanings should be capitalized and the contexts that justify capitalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of juridical acts and names
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Acts, juridical, capitalization of names of, 18.' (index entry)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rules for capitalizing names of statutes, legal acts, and similar juridical titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting 'A.D.' (anno Domini)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'A.D. (anno Domini): spacing of, 52, 210; use of small caps for, 52.' (index entry)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify spacing conventions around 'A.D.' and recommended use of small caps when setting the abbreviation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of titles in direct address and address-line formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Address, capitalization of titles in direct, 21. Address line: at end of letters, etc., how to set, 50; at opening of letters, etc., how to set, 64; omission of comma after, 161.' (index entries)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give detailed guidance on how to capitalize titles in direct address, how to set address lines at the opening and closing of letters, and punctuation (e.g., whether to include a comma after the address line).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization and quotation style for titles of addresses and publications
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Addresses, titles of: capitalization of principal words in, 41; to be roman-quoted, 82.' (index entry)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise capitalization of principal words in titles of addresses and indicate whether such titles should be set roman and placed in quotes (roman-quoted), with section references for specifics.
